result.summary: Enables safe identical code folding (ICF) linker flags in CMakeLists.txt when supported by the linker and compiler. The build system probes for and appends -faddrsig alongside -Wl,--icf=safe or -Wl,--icf=safe_thunks to executable linker flags.
result.problem: macOS release binaries contain redundant copies of identical compiled functions, increasing download sizes and disk footprint without functional benefit.
evidence: Author measurements in the description and commit message show binary size reductions of '~0.5mb' for bitcoind and '1.3mb' for bitcoin-qt on aarch64-apple-darwin.
result.changed_since_previous: Appended the -faddrsig compiler/linker flag to the ICF test strings to ensure address significance tables are emitted so safe ICF does not fold address-taken functions.
result.card: This pull request configures safe identical code folding linker flags (-Wl,--icf=safe / -Wl,--icf=safe_thunks with -faddrsig) in CMakeLists.txt. It reduces Darwin release binary sizes, saving roughly 0.5 MB on bitcoind and 1.3 MB on bitcoin-qt according to the author. The change primarily benefits macOS users downloading release binaries.

risk.why: Incorrect linker code folding could violate C++ function pointer uniqueness semantics or cause linking regressions across toolchains.
